value.body: Chartered Accountancy is a professional qualification, not a university degree. It is awarded by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), a statutory body. You move through three exam levels — Foundation, Intermediate and Final — with two years of practical training (articleship) before the Final. Qualified CAs work in audit, tax, accounting and finance, and only members in practice can sign a company's statutory audit.

items.label: Exam levels
items.note: Foundation → Intermediate → Final; exams held in January, May and September

items.label: Articleship
items.note: Starts after passing both Intermediate groups and the ICITSS course

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Register with ICAI for the Foundation course and sit the Foundation exam after Class 12; any stream can apply. Graduates with the required marks, and those who have passed the ICSI or ICMAI Intermediate level, can register directly for the Intermediate level.

value.title: At a glance
items: Pass rates at each level are low, and many students take more than one attempt per level.
Articleship is paid a stipend and gives real audit and tax work before you qualify.
Many students complete a B.Com or another degree by distance alongside the CA course.
Since 2021, UGC treats the CA qualification as equivalent to a postgraduate degree (for example, for NET and PhD).

value.title: CA Final pass rate, both groups
value.note: Candidates who sat both Final groups in the same attempt.
